title: dev-local.sh duplicates start:anvil's flags inline, so editing the start:anvil key no longer reaches `npm run dev`
severityRationale: Pure QA drift surface with no current consequence — the two are byte-identical today. Filed because it was newly created by this delta and is silent by construction: nothing fails, the two just diverge.
description: dev-local.sh:69 starts anvil directly rather than via `npm run start:anvil`, for a good and documented reason: `$!` must be anvil's own pid or the listener-ownership comparison at :110 and the trap at :36 would both be meaningless. The consequence is that the flag string now exists in two places, and package.json's `start:anvil` key — left byte-identical on purpose — is no longer on `dev`'s path.
failureScenario: A developer needs the local chain to mine instantly instead of every 2 seconds, or needs more pre-funded accounts, or wants to point the local stack at a fork. They edit the obvious place — the `start:anvil` key in package.json — confirm it by running `npm run start:anvil` directly, and see the new behaviour. They then run `npm run dev` and get the OLD configuration, with no error and no warning, because dev-local.sh:69 carries its own copy of the flags. Debugging starts from the false premise that the flag change did not take effect at all.
impact: A future change to the anvil configuration made in the obvious place (the `start:anvil` npm key: a different chain id, a `--fork-url`, a `--block-time` change, extra accounts) silently does not apply to `npm run dev`, and the two local environments diverge without any error.
recommendation: Keep the direct launch (the pid reasoning is correct) but stop duplicating the string: define the flags once — e.g. an `ANVIL_FLAGS` value sourced from a single file that `start:anvil` also uses, or have dev-local.sh read the flags out of package.json — or, at minimum, add a comment on the `start:anvil` key pointing at dev-local.sh:69 so an editor of either is told about the other.

dedup.reasoning: dev-local.sh is new in this delta (story-081), so no prior entry can cover it. Deliberately NOT collapsed with DEDUP-29-07 despite sharing the file: this is a configuration-duplication drift hazard in the anvil LAUNCH line, DEDUP-29-07 is a signal-delivery defect in the trap/cleanup path. Same file is not a root cause. Flagged as the weakest of the seven for triage judgement - see flaggedForReview.

validity.law3: non-malicious developer assumed; no malicious-dev framing present in this finding (grep-verified across the candidate set)
validity.footgunTest: borderline: duplicated anvil flags between start:anvil and dev-local.sh is a drift hazard a competent developer WOULD be surprised by (editing start:anvil no longer reaches `dev`), so it is kept - but it sits closest to the QA line and is flagged for human triage
validity.localOnlyNotASuppressionGround: `dev` is a local rehearsal harness on a throwaway anvil chain; the harm channel is FALSE ASSURANCE about a mainnet cutover, which is legitimate. Local-only was not used as a suppression ground.

label: Q-03

attackPath: No attacker. Maintainability drift path, with no current divergence:
1. A developer wants instant mining, more pre-funded accounts, or a fork target.
2. They edit the obvious place - the `start:anvil` key in package.json - and confirm it with `npm run start:anvil`.
3. `npm run dev` uses the OLD configuration, silently, because dev-local.sh:69 carries its own copy of the flags.
4. Debugging starts from the false premise that the flag change did not take effect at all.
classification.likelihood: low; requires someone to change anvil configuration at all.
classification.assumptions: The two strings, byte-identical today, are allowed to diverge.

classifierJustification: MOVED DOWN, low -> qa. The auditor's own severityRationale calls it 'pure QA drift surface with no current consequence' and its dedup block flags it as the weakest of the seven, sitting closest to the QA line - and on the merits that assessment is right, so the label should match it. There is no divergence today (the strings are byte-identical), no execution consequence, and no defect: the direct launch is CORRECT and deliberate, because `$!` must be anvil's own pid for the listener-ownership check at :110 and the trap at :36 to mean anything. What remains is a duplicated configuration string, which is a maintainability hazard. That is the textbook QA band, and calling it Low alongside four findings with concrete, reproduced execution consequences dilutes them. Moving it to QA is a labelling correction, NOT a drop: it stays in the report, in the QA bundle, with its failureScenario and recommendation intact, so Law-1 recall is fully preserved and a human can still triage it up at /ledger.
caveatsForHuman: This is a severity move, not a suppression. The finding is retained in full. Dropping it would have been the report-tidiness trade Law 1 forbids; re-labelling it to the band its own rationale describes is not that trade.

The minimum acceptable remedy is the cheapest one in the recommendation: a comment on the `start:anvil` key pointing at dev-local.sh:69. If only one thing is done, do that - it converts a silent divergence into a visible one.
Do NOT collapse with L-07 (DEDUP-29-07). Same file is not a root cause: this is configuration duplication in the anvil LAUNCH line, that is signal delivery in the trap/cleanup path.
